summary: Android port: MilestoneDto.nextOccurrence compares the milestone's local midnight with the current instant, so from 00:01 on the milestone day the next occurrence is a year away; the Milestones row computes days from the instant (day before reads 0d, day itself reads 364d) and NotificationPlanner drops the 9 AM 'today' ping when a reschedule runs that morning. Same defect as the iOS bug fixed on this branch (android/app/src/main/java/com/jackwallner/bond/model/Completion.kt:63, ui/screens/Milestones.kt:139).

iOS and Android: 'Reschedule' / 'Pick a time' on a partner's request cannot be saved. The editor upserts the partner-authored row (ReminderEditorView.save, repo.upsert; Android Reminders.kt PartnerRequestCard onEdit, ReminderEditor.kt:203), but supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql only lets the author write: reminders_member_insert needs author_id = auth.uid() and reminders_author_update / reminders_author_delete are author-only, and no later migration changes them. The target's save therefore fails with a row-level security error shown in the form, and a swipe-delete on a partner request removes the row locally while the server keeps it (it returns on the next refresh). Proven against the checked-in schema; not run against a database (no Postgres on the fleet host, production may differ).
guard: proposed: a database test (pgTAP or a two-user script against a local Supabase) that signs in as the target of a reminder authored by the partner and expects a reschedule to succeed and a delete to be refused with an error. Fix needs a product call: a SECURITY DEFINER rpc reschedule_reminder(p_id, p_fire_at) limited to the target (and handled/dismiss for deletes), or the editor writes an own copy; the client then calls it instead of upsert for partner-authored rows

summary: iOS: a reminder written for the partner only reaches their phone if their app runs between its creation and its time. Reminders become local notifications armed on the target's phone from the list that app fetched (NotificationScheduler.reschedule arms targetId == self only), and the list is only fetched while the app is open (launch, return to the foreground, pull to refresh, the realtime feed). Nothing registers for remote notifications (no registerForRemoteNotifications call, no aps-environment entitlement, profiles.apns_token is never written), so SupabaseFunctions/send-push has no token to send to, and there is no background refresh. 'Surprise (hidden from partner)' reminders can never be armed at all: reminders_member_select hides the row from the target. The editor, the templates (which target the partner for paired users), the watch and the marketing copy ('Set nudges for your partner') present partner delivery as working. docs/MVP_TRIAGE.md B3 already records it and offers shipping local-only with a caveat; the app has no caveat. Android documents the same limit (.claude/rules/android.md, 'Not ported').
guard: proposed: needs a product call first. If push ships: a test that a partner-targeted insert produces an APNs request for the target's stored token (send-push) and that the app registers and stores apns_token after the notification permission is granted. If it does not ship: copy in the editor and on the partner picker that the partner is nudged when their app next opens, and hide 'Surprise (hidden from partner)'
